title: Go-live Commander Briefing & Fallback Roster
summary: Field-ready commander brief for day-of launch. Includes prioritized KPIs, escalation matrix, surge triggers, and a 1-page fallback roster for quick reassignment. Written as a working-runbook for product ops and SRE leads.
objectives: Provide a single-sheet operational view for go-live commander during initial 72 hours
Define clear alert thresholds, decision points, and owner handoffs for launch-related incidents
List compact fallback assignments so that coverage can be restored within 15 minutes
Document minimal rollback criteria and communication steps to product, sales, and customers
commander_runway_timeline: T-48h: Final canary config snapshot + golden traffic sample (owner: Marco Ruiz)
T-6h: Confirm Dedicated pool capacity and burst limits; verify autoscale knobs (owner: Jinsoo Park)
T-30m: Slack channel staffed, PagerDuty rota confirmed, stakeholder readout (commander leads)
T+0 to T+3h: Gradual ramp: 0% -> 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% traffic (10m intervals for first two ramps)
T+24h: First health audit and KPI review; consider reducing observability retention if cost spike noted
T+72h: Stabilization checkpoint and canary rollback window closes unless new issues appear
critical_kpis_and_alerts: API availability (user-facing success rate): target >= 99.9% over 15m; page if < 99.5%
Generation error rate (model-side exceptions): alert at >= 0.5% over 5m
Median token latency (P50): target < 70ms; notify if > 150ms
Tail latency (P95): target < 350ms; page SRE if > 700ms
GPU utilization per pool: healthy 55-85%; page if sustained <40% (underprovision) or >90% (saturation)
KV cache hit rate: target >= 20% for repeat prefixes; warn if <8% after 1h
Unit cost burn (hosted): daily burn vs forecast > +25% triggers cost inspection (owner: Olivia Grant)
Throughput (requests/s): compare to expected ramp curve; deviation >30% for 30m triggers investigation
escalation_matrix: Commander: Asha Patel — primary decision maker for traffic/ramp/rollback (Slack: @asha, mobile: +1-415-555-0123)
SRE Lead: Jinsoo Park — infrastructure, autoscale, networking (pager: RDW-oncall)
Runtime Engineer: Marco Ruiz — model variants, fallback routing, canary toggles
Product Ops SM: Olivia Grant — customer comms, stakeholder updates, incident notes
Solutions Eng: Diego Fernandez — enterprise customer liaison and special-case routing
Legal/Compliance (on-call): Sarita Mehta — for data, privacy, or contractual incidents
Escalation rule: if commander unreachable for >10m, SRE Lead assumes commander role
fallback_roster: If primary runtime node pool saturated: switch canary traffic to quantized model variant (marco/action-override)
If Dedicated capacity degrades: enable burst-to-hosted policy for affected customer segments (jinsoo/enable-burst)
If hosted API cost unexpectedly spikes: throttle non-critical background eval jobs and lower observability retention (olivia/cost-throttle)
If persistent model quality regression detected: route traffic to previous pinned model version and freeze rollouts (commander/roll-back-model)
Hot swap contacts: list of 3 engineers per role in private doc (see linked_artifacts); aim to replace absent owner within 15 minutes
surge_capacity_triggers: Trigger A (soft): sustained traffic > 150% of expected for 10m — autoscale to +20% capacity and notify commander
Trigger B (hard): sustained traffic > 250% of expected for 5m — run emergency burst policy and consider traffic shaping
Trigger C (customer-SLA): single customer causing >30% of capacity — isolate to a throttled pool and notify account team
Manual override: commander can initiate pre-authorized cloud spin-up for dedicated pools (requires 2-minute approval window)
rollback_criteria: Severity-based rollback: any user-facing P95 latency > 700ms for 30m and error rate >1% triggers rollback decision meeting
Quality-based rollback: A/B eval shows >5% drop in key accuracy metric vs baseline for 1h
Cost-based rollback: sustained unit cost > +40% vs forecast for 6h without clear remediation
Partial rollback allowed: can roll back model for specific region or customer tier while keeping others live
communication_playbook: Internal alert: Slack #go-live-command with short header (what, where, impact, owner) within 2 minutes of detection
Stakeholder update cadence: 15m during incident, 1h if resolved but monitoring continues, daily summary at EOD
Customer comms: product ops drafts customer-safe message and routes to account team for approval (template in Confluence)
Public status: update status.redwood.ai if user-visible degradation >15 minutes; include mitigation steps and ETA
Post-incident: ensure blameless postmortem posted within 72h with remediation owners
rehearsal_tasks: Run a 30m tabletop with commander + SRE + runtime engineer one week pre-launch
Execute a scripted canary rollback in staging and time the full rollback path end-to-end
Validate PagerDuty rota and confirm mobile reachability for all listed owners
Simulate a cost spike by enabling synthetic traffic and confirm cost alerting chain
Confirm page playbook snippets are pinned in #ops and that oncall acknowledges the runbook
post_launch_review_triggers: Any incident that caused >1 hour user-facing downtime
Any change that required cross-team rollback
Cost deviation >25% from forecast for first 7 days
quick_commands_and_slack_snippets: Commander alert: /msg #go-live-command "Commander: Asha Patel — initiating 30% rollback to stable model; see link: <runbook>"
Customer notice (template): "We are aware of elevated latency and actively mitigating; next update in 30m."
notes: This doc is intentionally concise — keep it to one page for the commander dashboard (expandables live in Confluence)
During the first 4 hours prioritize availability over cost; after 24h revert to normal cost guardrails
If a third-party dependency (cloud region or partner) is implicated, tag PartnerOps and Account Execs immediately
Action items from rehearsal: confirm quantized fallback image checksum, publish canary golden sample to S3
